paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish. (A tanna of a baraita.)

In [Kohelet Rabbah 1:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.1.15.2) we find Yehudah ben Lakish teaching in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel. In the Sifra, Acharei, at the printed locator קלא, the attribution is given as “רש״בג in the name of רש״בל.” Hyman regards this as an error: he proposes that it should read “Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish says in the name of רש״בג,” citing Yalkut Joshua, remez 23, in support.[^1]

He is also mentioned in baraitot: Shabbat 43; Yoma 53b and 85; Chagigah 9; and in Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, chapter 1, halakhah 1; Mekhilta, Yitro, Parashat BaChodesh, chapter 1; and Tosefta Sotah, chapter 7.[^2]

notes.text: The corresponding digital [Sifra, Acharei Mot 8:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra,_Acharei_Mot,_Section_8.7) reads “Shimon ben Gamliel in the name of Shimon ben Lakish.” [Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 23:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.23.6) instead has “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in the name of Yehudah ben Lakish.” Both run in the opposite direction to Hyman’s proposed replacement; the second name also differs. The Kohelet passage titles Shimon ben Gamliel Rabbi, while the Yalkut calls him Rabban.
The printed marks leave the sides of Shabbat 43, Yoma 85 and Chagigah 9 unspecified. Yoma 53b has an explicit side marker.
